===== FILE 20800__1.pdf =====
September 3, 2025 
Dr. Steven L. Lieberman 
Acting Under Secretary for Health 
Department of Veterans Affairs 
810 Vermont Avenue NW,  
Washington, DC 20420 
 
RE: “Reproductive Health Services,” [VA-2025-VHA-0073)] 
Dear Dr. Lieberman:  
On behalf of Advancing American Freedom (AAF), we are writing to file a comment in response 
to the Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) proposed rule, “Reproductive Health Services.” We 
applaud the VA’s efforts to ensure the VA only provides “needed” medical services to American 
heroes. 
The VA’s proposed rule is not revolutionary, but it is laudable. From 1999 when the VA 
established the “medical benefits package” until the Biden Administration’s craven response to 
Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health in September 2022, the VA did not include abortion in the 
“medical benefits package” because it was not a “needed” medical service. 
Further, for twenty years, every secretary and administration accepted the determination that 
abortion was not a “needed” service for veterans. That changed during the Biden Administration, 
which expanded federal abortion funding claiming to anticipate an increased need for abortion in 
the wake of Dobbs. The anticipated increase never materialized. 
AAF has fought the harm to which government agencies have exposed women through chemical 
abortions.1 Playing politics with dangerous chemical abortion drugs undermines the public health 
goals these agencies are supposed to strive for.  
Opponents to the VA’s proposed rule twist the definition of “illness” and “condition”2 as did the 
FDA when it approved mifepristone for use as an abortifacient.3 Pregnancy is not a serious 
medical condition that is “solved” by abortion. While women may experience complications, 
pregnancy itself is not a problem. 
 
1 See AAF Comment in (FDA-2025-P-0377-0001)  
2 For just a few examples, see https://www.regulations.gov/comment/VA-2025-VHA-0073-9413; 
https://www.regulations.gov/comment/VA-2025-VHA-0073-19967; https://www.regulations.gov/comment/VA-
2025-VHA-0073-4838; https://www.regulations.gov/comment/VA-2025-VHA-0073-15483 
3 For more on the FDA’s  treating the “termination of an unwanted pregnancy” as a “serious condition” to be 
addressed by mifepristone see J. Marc Wheat and Timothy Harper, “Playing Politics with the Abortion Pill: A 
Quarter Century of Abuse of Power at the FDA,” Human Life Review Volume LI, no. 2 (Spring 2025): 61-72, 
https://humanlifereview.com/issue/spring-2025/. 

We applaud the VA’s proposed rule to restore the definition of “needed medical benefits” to 
exclude abortions and abortion counseling.  
  
J. Marc Wheat 
 
 
 
 
 
 
General Counsel  
 
 
 
 
 
  
Advancing American Freedom  
 
 
 
  
Vice President Mike Pence, Founder
